title: Parameters from a scheme at a rational point of a smooth algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $k$ a field [def-weil-field] over $S$. Let $U/S$ be a scheme, $u\in U$ a closed point, $E/k$ an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] smooth over $k$, and $p:E\to U$ an $S$-morphism. Smooth and etale morphisms of spaces are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to E$ is a $k$-rational point with image $u$ under $p$, the induced map $\kappa(u)\to k$ is an isomorphism, and $E\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ has dimension zero at $z$. For a space $H$, dimension at a point is dimension on an etale scheme chart, with scheme dimension at a point the infimum of dimensions of its open neighbourhoods. There are an affine open neighbourhood $U'\subset U$ of $u$, an integer $d\geq0$, functions $f_1,\ldots,f_d\in\Gamma(U',\mathcal O_{U'})$ vanishing at $u$, an etale scheme chart $V\to p^{-1}(U')$ and a point $v\in V$ above $z$, such that their pullbacks form an $\mathcal O_{V,v}$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. If $Z=V(f_1,\ldots,f_d)\subset U'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], then $\dim_z(E\times_U Z)=0$. The point $z$ belongs to this fibre product. The empty sequence is allowed.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U_0$ of $u$ and an etale scheme atlas $V\to p^{-1}(U_0)$. Its pullback along $z$ is a nonempty etale scheme over $k$, by the definition of a representable etale atlas. Choose a point of that pullback and write $v$ for its image in $V$. Since $z$ is $k$-rational, its residue field is $k$, so the pullback point has residue field $\kappa(v)$. On an affine open of the pullback, the etale residue-field lemma gives $\kappa(v)/k$ finite separable. By the chart convention of the statement $V/k$ is smooth, hence locally of finite type. Choose a finite-type affine open $W\subset V$ containing $v$. The closed-point criterion over a field shows that $v$ is closed in $W$. We retain $V$ as the atlas; only the local calculations are made on $W$.

source.place: Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field); stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06MF, ordinary etale-chart version of the local-ring setup

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{V,v}=\mathcal O_{W,v}$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the local map induced by $p$. The smooth-scheme regularity theorem applied to the smooth $k$-scheme $V$ makes $B$ a nonzero regular local ring, in particular Noetherian. Apply the regular-local depth theorem with the empty regular sequence: it gives $\operatorname{depth}(B)=\dim B$, so $B$ is Cohen--Macaulay. The finite-dimension theorem for Noetherian local rings gives a finite integer $d=\dim B\ge0$. This step imposes no Noetherian or finite-type assumption on $U$ or $A$.

source.place: Tag 06MF, regularity and Cohen--Macaulay paragraph; varieties.tex Tag 056S; algebra.tex Tags 00NQ and 00KQ

proof.text: Let $I=\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B$. The local ring of $V\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ at the point over $v$ is $B/I$: on affine charts the fibre-product formula is a tensor product, and $D\otimes_R\kappa(u)=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}D/\mathfrak p(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}D$; localization at the chosen prime gives $B/\mathfrak m_AB$. Here $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $u$ corresponds to $\mathfrak p$, and $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset W$ is an affine neighbourhood of $v$. The hypothesis on $E\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ and the etale-chart convention give dimension zero at this chart point. Every prime chain in its local ring is a chain of generalizations of the point and lies in every open neighbourhood of it. Its length is therefore at most that neighbourhood dimension, hence at most zero. Thus $B/I$ is a nonzero local ring of dimension zero, whose only prime is its maximal ideal. Taking inverse images of primes in $B\to B/I$ gives $\sqrt I=\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 06MF, kernel calculation and radical equality in the local-ring paragraph

proof.text: Apply the image-selection lemma to $\varphi:A\to B$, using the Cohen--Macaulay equality of step 2 and the radical equality of step 3. It supplies $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in\mathfrak m_A$ whose images $b_i=\varphi(a_i)$ form a $B$-regular sequence. The Cohen--Macaulay regular-sequence dimension criterion, applied with $r=d$, gives $\dim B/(b_1,\ldots,b_d)=d-d=0$. Its hypotheses hold because $B$ is Noetherian local of finite dimension, $\operatorname{depth}(B)=d$, and all $b_i$ lie in $\mathfrak m_B$ by locality of $\varphi$.

Each $a_i\in A$ is the germ of a function on some open neighbourhood of $u$. Intersect these finitely many neighbourhoods and choose an affine open $u\in U'\subset U_0$ inside the intersection. Restrict the representatives to get $f_i\in\Gamma(U',\mathcal O_{U'})$. Their residues at $u$ vanish because $a_i\in\mathfrak m_A$. Replace $V$ by $V\times_U U'$; this is an open part of $V$, still an etale atlas of $p^{-1}(U')$, and its local ring at $v$ is still $B$. The pulled-back germs are exactly the $b_i$, so they remain a regular sequence. Set $Z=V(f_1,\ldots,f_d)\subset U'$. Every $f_i$ pulls back to zero on $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to E$, since evaluation factors through $\kappa(u)\cong k$. Consequently $z$ factors through $E\times_U Z$. With $d=0$ use any affine $U'$ as above and $Z=U'$; all these assertions retain their meaning.

source.place: Tag 06MF, spreading the finitely many germs and forming the closed slice

proof.text: The pullback chart $V_Z=V\times_U Z\to E\times_U Z$ is etale, by the base-change clause in the definition of the representable etale atlas. On the affine open $W\cap p^{-1}(U')$ near $v$, shrink once more to a finite-type affine $k$-neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}D'$. Its intersection with $V_Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(D'/(p^*f_1,\ldots,p^*f_d))$, again a finite-type $k$-scheme. The point $v$ is closed there, since it was closed in $W$. Localizing this quotient at $v$ gives $B/(b_1,\ldots,b_d)$: explicitly $(D'/J)_{\mathfrak q/J}=D'_{\mathfrak q}/JD'_{\mathfrak q}$ for $J=(p^*f_i)$ and the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $v$. Its dimension is zero by step 4. The closed-point dimension theorem now gives $\dim_v V_Z=0$. By the dimension convention in the item, computed on this etale chart, $\dim_z(E\times_U Z)=\dim_v V_Z=0$. This proves the remaining conclusion.
